title: Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements Earning by Fare Brand on Card-Paid Segments
content:
The fare brand of a card-paid ticket booked under a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement decides how the flown segment's company points are earned. The fare brand is the one on the ticket's record in Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.

The starting figure is the standard card-paid segment points: the segment's eligible spend multiplied by the tier's points per dollar, rounded down to the whole point. The earned card-paid segment points then follow the brand:

| Fare brand of the card-paid ticket | Earned card-paid segment points |
|---|---|
| Crestline Premium Economy or Crestline First | the standard card-paid segment points multiplied by 2 |
| Crestline Main Flexible or Crestline Main Plus | the standard card-paid segment points with 250 points added |
| any other fare brand | the standard card-paid segment points as they are |

### Examples (hypothetical standard points of 459)

- Crestline Premium Economy: 459 multiplied by 2 gives 918 earned points.
- Crestline First: likewise 918.
- Crestline Main Plus: 459 with 250 added gives 709.
- Crestline Main Flexible: likewise 709.
- Crestline Main Cabin: 459, as they are.

### Notes

- The multiplier of 2 and the addition of 250 are applied to whole points already rounded down; no further rounding arises from them.
- The 250 points are added once per segment, not once per ticket: a round trip in Crestline Main Plus has two segments, and each earns its own 250.
